name: PostgreSQL
model: Tables of rows queried with SQL; also JSONB documents, arrays, full-text search, and extensions such as pgvector and PostGIS
engine_note: Heap tables plus B-tree (and GIN, GiST, BRIN) indexes; MVCC by keeping old row versions, cleaned up later by VACUUM; write-ahead log
consistency: Multi-row transactions. Default isolation read committed; repeatable read (really snapshot isolation) and serializable are options. Commit waits for the WAL to be flushed to disk by default. Streaming replicas are asynchronous by default, so replica reads can be stale.

jepsen.finding: If the network drops the commit acknowledgement, the client cannot know whether its transaction committed; a property of any client-server commit, not a Postgres bug.
Serializable on a single node allowed G2-item anomalies (a bug in conflict detection, present since 9.5); fixed in the 2020-08-13 minor releases.

RDS Multi-AZ clusters violated snapshot isolation (Long Fork) when reading from replicas; root cause is how stock Postgres replicas decide transaction visibility, so it applies to Postgres replication generally; unresolved at publication.

scaling: Bigger machine first; add read replicas (streaming replication) for reads; no built-in sharding, so write scale-out needs Citus, application sharding, or a distributed SQL system.
version_note: PostgreSQL 19 was still in beta (Beta 4 announced 2026-09-24), so 18.6 is the latest stable release on 2026-10-04.
reach: Reach for it when you need users, orders, chats or anything relational with real transactions and constraints, on one machine up to several TB.
avoid: Avoid when write volume outgrows one primary, when you need multi-region writes, or for petabyte analytics scans.
escape: It is the default the others are escapes from.
chat: Users, chats, messages, API keys and billing rows; with pgvector, message embeddings too at modest scale.
notes: The 2013 aphyr.com post is blocked from the UK (HTTP 451); date 2013-05-18 read from the Wayback Machine copy. The RDS Multi-AZ cluster report is about RDS for PostgreSQL (two readable standbys), not Aurora; Jepsen argues the anomaly comes from stock Postgres replication visibility, so any Postgres primary plus hot standby reads can show it. Consistency facts are from the docs pages cited (synchronous_commit defaults to on; replication asynchronous by default).
